3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: It was low tide. The waves of the Antacean Sea lapped at the sands below the cliffs of Monqiz.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: A trail was carved into the cliffside, just wide enough for a single horse. Vina picked up speed as she guided her mare, Lizzie, around a sharp curve.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: She glanced back at me for just long enough to roll her eyes.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: Vina glanced back at me with a grin.

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: I watched her fly down the trail.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: At the bottom of the trail was a sheltered cove where Pabel had laid out a picnic lunch. I dismounted and sat down next to Vina.

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: She glanced back at me with a grin and gave the horse a swift kick in the side with her spurred boot.

14.speaker: Vina Toras
14.text: "You really didn't have to come back to Monqiz with me, Father."

15.speaker: Player_Romus
15.text: "I wanted to. It's been ages since we had time together."

16.speaker: Player_Romus
16.text: "I'm grateful for the break. It's too hectic in Porte Drazon."

17.speaker: Vina Toras
17.text: "We could be spending time at Palas Rezna. If you'd let me on the council, that is."

21.speaker: Player_Romus
21.text: "I wanted to. Council meetings don't exactly count as quality time together."

22.speaker: Vina Toras
22.text: "Deciding the fate of the country together? That screams quality time to me."

24.speaker: Vina Toras
24.text: "I like the place. But I can't let Lizzie think I've forgotten about her."

28.speaker: Vina Toras
28.text: "A Sordish resort in Monqiz! I can't believe you agreed to that."

29.speaker: Vina Toras
29.text: "Ah. I knew there was another reason."

30.speaker: Narrator
30.text: She picked up a lobster salad sandwich from the picnic basket and nibbled at it. A solemn silence descended as we stared out at the waves.

31.speaker: Vina Toras
31.text: "Eight years since she died. When I'm here, it might as well have been yesterday."

32.speaker: Vina Toras
32.text: "I can't even dip my toe in the water, or it'll all come rushing back."

33.speaker: Player_Romus
33.text: "I'd still declare you next in line. Rizia needs a queen like you, and the rules were meant to be broken."

34.speaker: Player_Romus
34.text: "He'd become my successor, of course. Those are the rules. But you'll still be a duchess."

38.speaker: Player_Romus
38.text: "You know what'll help blot out those memories? A big Sordish resort, right on this spot."

39.speaker: Player_Romus
39.text: "It'll get easier over time. It did for me."

40.speaker: Player_Romus
40.text: "Grief isn't a straight line, my daughter. It ebbs and flows like the tide."

41.speaker: Vina Toras
41.text: "It's always high tide for me. And I'm not sure I even want to come up for air."

42.speaker: Vina Toras
42.text: "But you must be feeling the same way about Mother. Otherwise, you would've remarried by now."

43.speaker: Player_Romus
43.text: "What makes you think our family will still hold power by the time I die?"
43.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Focus_Government_Reform"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Hugo_KnowsIntention"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true) == false

45.speaker: Vina Toras
45.text: "But you're a man. As long as your wife's young enough, you could have another child at any age."

52.speaker: Player_Romus
52.text: "I've got to do some glad-handing here anyway, before the Sordish invasion begins."

53.speaker: Player_Romus
53.text: "I just wanted to relish the sight of this beautiful, Sord-free beach."

54.speaker: Vina Toras
54.text: "A Sordish resort in Monqiz! I can't believe they thought you'd go for it."

58.speaker: Vina Toras
58.text: "Don't you think that's a little elitist? Beaches should belong to everyone."

59.speaker: Player_Romus
59.text: "You don't have anything to worry about. My childbearing days are over."

65.speaker: Vina Toras
65.text: "Like Queen Lyza said. The eldest sibling should inherit the throne, no matter their sex."

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: The tide was beginning to lap at the edge of our blanket. We stood up and pulled it away from the water.

70.speaker: Vina Toras
70.text: "But... Queen Lyza always said the eldest child should inherit the throne. No matter their sex."

71.speaker: Vina Toras
71.text: "Then let's see how many rules I can break once I'm queen."

72.speaker: Vina Toras
72.text: "The rules are the rules, I get it. No use being queen if the people don't want me, anyway."

73.speaker: Vina Toras
73.text: "Never mind. Who knows if it will even happen."

76.speaker: Player_Romus
76.text: "I'm not hungry right now. I'll eat my sandwich when we get back to the palace."

80.speaker: Vina Toras
80.text: "Grandmother is always on about how I need to find the right husband."

81.speaker: Vina Toras
81.text: "How important is it to you, really? Whom I marry?"

82.speaker: Player_Romus
82.text: "Why? Do you have any candidates in mind?"

83.speaker: Player_Romus
83.text: "Don't listen to that hypocrite. Grandma followed her heart, and so should you."

84.speaker: Vina Toras
84.text: "No, but do *you*? Are you going to marry me off, like your father did to you?"

85.speaker: Player_Romus
85.text: "I don't care whom you marry. As long as he's of noble birth, of course."

86.speaker: Player_Romus
86.text: "You're a princess, Vina. Your marriage status matters not only to me, but to the whole country."

87.speaker: Vina Toras
87.text: "Does that mean you're planning to marry me off? Like your father did to you?"

88.speaker: Vina Toras
88.text: "So you're not planning to marry me off. Like your father did to you."

90.speaker: Player_Romus
90.text: "My arranged marriage was the best thing that ever happened to me."

91.speaker: Player_Romus
91.text: "Absolutely not. Arranged marriage is a barbaric tradition."

95.speaker: Vina Toras
95.text: "I wasn't blind and deaf growing up. I don't want to end up like you and Mother."

96.speaker: Vina Toras
96.text: "You and Mother were lucky to fall in love. Most such marriages are miserable."

97.speaker: Player_Romus
97.text: "I might suggest a potential husband or two. But I'll never drag you to the altar."

99.speaker: Vina Toras
99.text: "You and Mother were living proof of that."

103.speaker: Vina Toras
103.text: "It worked out for you and Mother."

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: She fixed me with a stare.

105.speaker: Player_Romus
105.text: "You want to be queen? This is part of it. A single wedding can accomplish more than a hundred political conferences."

106.speaker: Player_Romus
106.text: "Relax. I might suggest a potential husband or two, but I'll never drag you to the altar."

107.speaker: Player_Romus
107.text: "Whether or not I loved her, I did what I was ordered to do. As you will when the day comes."

108.speaker: Vina Toras
108.text: "So you won't try to marry me off. Like your father did to you."

110.speaker: Player_Romus
110.text: "Think of it as yet another one of your royal obligations. You can always take a lover on the side."

111.speaker: Player_Romus
111.text: "I trust you to make the right decision. For yourself, and for Rizia."

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: She regarded me coolly for a moment.

116.speaker: Narrator
116.text: She mulled over my words for a moment.

120.speaker: Vina Toras
120.text: "That's the least I could ask of you. But good to know."

126.speaker: Narrator
126.text: Her expression was hard to read.

130.speaker: Vina Toras
130.text: "Let's hope that my heart and Rizia's needs align."

131.speaker: Vina Toras
131.text: "I appreciate your honesty. I do know we royals must make compromises in our personal lives."

132.speaker: Player_Romus
132.text: "We both loved you. And we both swore you'd never go through the same hell we did."

133.speaker: Player_Romus
133.text: "I don't know what you're talking about."

134.speaker: Player_Romus
134.text: "All because I didn't have the courage to speak to my father as an equal. You're braver than I was."

135.speaker: Player_Romus
135.text: "We made the best of the situation we'd been forced into."

136.speaker: Player_Romus
136.text: "I still wish I'd had a choice. The least I can do is grant you one."

139.speaker: Vina Toras
139.text: "That means a lot, Father. And it's a decision I won't take lightly."

140.speaker: Narrator
140.text: She regarded me coolly for a second.

141.speaker: Vina Toras
141.text: "I wasn't deaf or blind as a child, you know. I'm happy I won't have to subject my own to the same fate."

142.speaker: Vina Toras
142.text: "I hope someday I can have what you two had. Arranged or otherwise."

143.speaker: Narrator
143.text: I staggered through the doorway of Palas Monqiz, exhausted. Pabel swiftly took my coat.

148.speaker: Player_Romus
148.text: "She's too fast for her old man."

149.speaker: Player_Romus
149.text: "She's visiting with a friend, but she wanted to thank you for lunch."

150.speaker: Player_Romus
150.text: "In another castle. I let her go out, against my better judgement."

151.speaker: Pabel Adria
151.text: "I remember a certain Romus Toras being quite the rider himself."

152.speaker: Pabel Adria
152.text: "I heard you used to be quite the rider yourself."

153.speaker: Pabel Adria
153.text: "Monqiz lobster. It's never so sweet as when it's fresh out of the water."

157.speaker: Pabel Adria
157.text: "She's more than old enough to go out alone. You can't protect her from everything."

158.speaker: Pabel Adria
158.text: "Any daughter of King Romus is bound to have a strong will."

160.speaker: Player_Romus
160.text: "I'm not sore at all. But a bath sounds good."

163.speaker: Pabel Adria
163.text: "Let me know if you need anything else."

164.speaker: Pabel Adria
164.text: "Is there any other kind of bath?"

165.speaker: Narrator
165.text: I made my way to Palas Monqiz's master bathroom, where an enormous clawfoot tub was filled to the brim with soapy, eucalyptus-scented water. I undressed and got in.

170.speaker: Narrator
170.text: A tap came at the door, so soft I thought I was imagining it at first.

178.speaker: Pabel Adria
178.text: "I'll just be a second. I forgot to leave you a towel."

180.speaker: Player_Romus
180.text: "Don't you have anything better to do? Stop bothering me."

181.speaker: Pabel Adria
181.text: "Very well. Have a nice bath, Your Majesty."

187.speaker: Narrator
187.text: After a thorough soak, I dressed and headed to my study. I still had some work to go over before the trip back.

188.speaker: Narrator
188.text: I heard his footsteps receding in the hallway.

190.speaker: Narrator
190.text: She seemed to shrink a little.

191.speaker: Vina Toras
191.text: "Whatever you say, Father. I should be going now."

193.speaker: Narrator
193.text: She'd thrown herself into horseback riding after Lena died. We kept a few horses in Porte Drazon as well, but Lizzie was her favorite.

194.speaker: Narrator
194.text: I followed her at a leisurely pace, taking time to gaze back up the hill at Palas Monqiz. With Hubertus Toras governing the province from his own estate, I was free to visit my old home and its private beach anytime I liked.

195.speaker: Player_Romus
195.text: "We already discussed this. What have you been doing instead?"

196.speaker: Player_Romus
196.text: "I don't know how much we're deciding. Sometimes I feel like it's out of any of our hands."

197.speaker: Player_Romus
197.text: "My mother was right about a few things. It's not healthy to spend too long in those chambers."

198.speaker: Player_Romus
198.text: "Keep up that enthusiasm. It will serve you well when you're older."

199.speaker: Vina Toras
199.text: "The usual. Ballgoing. Public appearances. Grandmother enrolled me in an advanced etiquette class."

202.speaker: Player_Romus
202.text: "A Marcel Koronti resort on these shores would attract the worst kind of elitist. Trust me."

203.speaker: Vina Toras
203.text: "You're probably right. I've read about him and his horrible father."

204.speaker: Player_Romus
204.text: "Everyone in *Rizia*. The Sords have their own beaches."

205.speaker: Player_Romus
205.text: "Trust me, it's nowhere near as exciting as you imagine."

206.speaker: Vina Toras
206.text: "I'm sure it's more exciting than the etiquette class Grandmother made me start taking."

207.speaker: Player_Romus
207.text: "None of your backtalk. Let's just treasure what time we have."

208.speaker: Vina Toras
208.text: "Hectic for you, maybe. I'm bored to tears."

212.speaker: Vina Toras
212.text: "By the way, did you know it's considered polite to intentionally lose a Derdian Duel of Generosity?"

214.speaker: Player_Romus
214.text: "They made me drink whiskey. It went to my head."

217.speaker: Vina Toras
217.text: "Honestly... I probably would have let them have it. Lyza knew how valuable it was to be close to Sordland."

218.speaker: Player_Romus
218.text: "It was the right diplomatic move. I'm sure of it."

221.speaker: Vina Toras
221.text: "Not at all, Father. I'm sure you had your reasons."

222.speaker: Vina Toras
222.text: "No need to make excuses, Father. A King stands by his decisions."

224.speaker: Player_Romus
224.text: "I may have made the wrong diplomatic move, but it felt right in my heart."

225.speaker: Vina Toras
225.text: "No need to make excuses, Father. A King stands by his decisions."

226.speaker: Player_Romus
226.text: "They thought they could buy me with their greasy Sordish ren. I showed them."

228.speaker: Narrator
228.text: I looked out at the sea again.

234.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
234.text: Try not to think about it.

235.speaker: Narrator
235.text: The sickening sound the boat had made as its girders splintered. Calling out for my wife, over and over, until my voice finally gave out. The beep of the hospital machines as I told Vina to say goodbye to her mother one last time.

239.speaker: Narrator
239.text: Tears formed at the corners of my eyes.

241.speaker: Narrator
241.text: The sickening sound the boat had made as its girders splintered. Vina calling out for her mother, over and over, until her voice finally gave out. My daughter's eyes as I told her she would never see Lena again.

242.speaker: Narrator
242.text: It was just an ocean. A big, impartial ocean.

246.speaker: Narrator
246.text: The break in the coast guard's voice as he told me the news. The hospital staff muttering meaningless reassurances. The beep of the ventilator as my wife slipped in and out of consciousness.

248.speaker: Narrator
248.text: Was there anything I could have done to save her? In another timeline, were there three of us sitting on this beach instead of two?

252.speaker: Narrator
252.text: The break in the coast guard's voice as he told me the news. The hospital staff muttering meaningless reassurances. My daughter's eyes as I told her she would never see her mother again.

253.speaker: Narrator
253.text: If I had been on that boat, would things have gone differently? In another timeline, were there three of us sitting on this beach instead of two?

254.speaker: Narrator
254.text: Worst of all: the secret relief I felt when the hospital ventilator beeped for the last time.

261.speaker: Narrator
261.text: She cast a sidelong glance at me.

263.speaker: Narrator
263.text: She let out a sound that was half-laugh, half-sniffle.

264.speaker: Vina Toras
264.text: "Then why haven't you remarried? You must know it's unusual for a king to stay a widower for so long."

265.speaker: Vina Toras
265.text: "If you're so keen to forget her, why haven't you remarried?"

267.speaker: Player_Romus
267.text: "We've got to move forward. Lena wouldn't have wanted us to stay in mourning for so long."

268.speaker: Vina Toras
268.text: "Are you... are you thinking of moving forward, Father?"

269.speaker: Vina Toras
269.text: "Eight years and not so much as a date."

270.speaker: Player_Romus
270.text: "Don't be naive. I've had dates. Just nobody worth telling you about."

271.speaker: Player_Romus
271.text: "What's with the sudden interest in my love life?"

272.speaker: Player_Romus
272.text: "It feels useless to try. I'll never love anyone else as much as I loved your mother."

273.speaker: Player_Romus
273.text: "Looking after you has been my number-one priority."

278.speaker: Narrator
278.text: Vina gave me a small smile.

280.speaker: Narrator
280.text: Her face went through a few different expressions as she quietly processed this information.

281.speaker: Vina Toras
281.text: "You can't use that as an excuse for much longer."

283.speaker: Narrator
283.text: She nervously picked up a handful of sand and let it run through her fingers.

284.speaker: Narrator
284.text: Vina appeared at a loss for words. She tentatively put a hand on my shoulder.

285.speaker: Vina Toras
285.text: "I'm sorry, Father. I didn't realize it was still so fresh for you as well."

287.speaker: Player_Romus
287.text: "She's in a better place now, Vina. As you and I will be one day."

288.speaker: Narrator
288.text: My daughter didn't join me, but maintained a respectful silence.

290.speaker: Vina Toras
290.text: "Me too. But it's got to get easier sometime, right?"

292.speaker: Vina Toras
292.text: "Maybe not. But I can't help it."

294.speaker: Vina Toras
294.text: "And you can't stay a widower forever."

295.speaker: Vina Toras
295.text: "But what happens until then? We're just supposed to keep going like nothing happened?"

298.speaker: Vina Toras
298.text: "But then... if you *were* to meet someone..."

301.speaker: Narrator
301.text: She nervously picked up a handful of sand and let it run through her fingers.

303.speaker: Vina Toras
303.text: "What if you had a son? Who would be your successor when you died?"

304.speaker: Vina Toras
304.text: "Thank you, Father. It means a lot to know all my preparation won't be for nothing."

305.speaker: Player_Romus
305.text: "Fine, you can bring Lizzie back to Porte Drazon. But you'll have to get rid of one of your other horses to make room in the stables."

306.speaker: Vina Toras
306.text: "Oh, that'd be grand! But I wanted to ask something else."

307.speaker: Vina Toras
307.text: "Sorry to run, but one of the countesses from my school days has invited me for tea. She's just a few estates down the beach from here."

308.speaker: Player_Romus
308.text: "But I thought we'd be spending the whole visit together."

309.speaker: Player_Romus
309.text: "Have fun. I'm glad we were able to talk."

310.speaker: Player_Romus
310.text: "Titus! Send one of your men to keep an eye on her?"

311.speaker: Narrator
311.text: My guard appeared from behind a rock.

316.speaker: Vina Toras
316.text: "I've spent enough time with you, I think."

317.speaker: Vina Toras
317.text: "Don't worry. I'll be back before supper."

321.speaker: Player_Romus
321.text: "Try and gauge her reaction to the Sordish resort idea, will you?"

322.speaker: Narrator
322.text: She rode away before I could think of a comeback.

329.speaker: Vina Toras
329.text: "I won't get into trouble. But I understand the need for protocol."

330.speaker: Vina Toras
330.text: "No need. I already know her family hates it."

334.speaker: Vina Toras
334.text: "I already know her family hates it. But I'll try to sway them for you."

335.speaker: Narrator
335.text: The trip back up to the palace felt a lot longer than the way down. It was dusk by the time I'd returned my horse to the stables.

342.speaker: Pabel Adria
342.text: "Back so soon? I hope I packed enough food for you."

344.speaker: Pabel Adria
344.text: "There's a warm bath waiting for you upstairs, in case you're sore from the ride."

345.speaker: Pabel Adria
345.text: "May I come in? I forgot to leave you a towel."

346.speaker: Player_Romus
346.text: "It's not important. I'll dry off without one."

350.speaker: Player_Romus
350.text: "I told you not to come in, Pabel."

353.speaker: Player_Romus
353.text: "It's time for the people of Rizia to hold the real power, Vina."

354.speaker: Player_Romus
354.text: "The monarchy must die if Rizia is to enter the modern era. At least in its current form."

355.speaker: Player_Romus
355.text: "We stopped one uprising. I fear the next won't be so easy to suppress."

357.speaker: Player_Romus
357.text: "We would stay on, but only in a symbolic role. The human embodiment of Rizian grace and dignity."

358.speaker: Player_Romus
358.text: "We could do anything we wanted! All the riches, none of the responsibility. Isn't that the dream?"

359.speaker: Player_Romus
359.text: "We'd live as normal citizens. We don't deserve to be treated as superior simply by virtue of our birth."

361.speaker: Player_Romus
361.text: "We would still perform some important duties. But a democratically elected leader should do the real work of governing the country."

363.speaker: Vina Toras
363.text: "I understand. But I always thought I'd be more than that."

364.speaker: Vina Toras
364.text: "Maybe for you. I always thought my life would be more than that."

368.speaker: Vina Toras
368.text: "You know, Queen Lyza likened the monarchy to a steady ship on a stormy ocean. We provide stability and comfort, even during the most unpredictable of times."

369.speaker: Vina Toras
369.text: "You know, this book I'm reading likened monarchy to a leaky old galleon -- weighed down by the anchor of tradition, steered only by inertia and the whims of a privileged few."

374.speaker: Player_Romus
374.text: "How are you still reading that? I took it away."

375.speaker: Player_Romus
375.text: "You're still reading that? Even after I banned Malenyevist propaganda?"

376.speaker: Player_Romus
376.text: "That's cruel to those of us who are only trying to keep our country afloat."

377.speaker: Player_Romus
377.text: "Maybe it's time to sink that ship."

379.speaker: Vina Toras
379.text: "Maybe we're dead weight. We have to sink so the rest of the country can swim."

380.speaker: Vina Toras
380.text: "Well... um, yes. He makes a lot of good points."

385.speaker: Vina Toras
385.text: "You can't stop me from informing myself, Father. And he makes a lot of good points."

386.speaker: Player_Romus
386.text: "She was right. We're not ready to sink to the bottom of the ocean just yet."

387.speaker: Player_Romus
387.text: "Wise words. But the Rizian people should steer their own ship."

388.speaker: Player_Romus
388.text: "I am warning you, Vina. Stop filling your head with this nonsense."

389.speaker: Player_Romus
389.text: "I don't know, His concept of vanguardism doesn't sound too far off from monarchy to me."

390.speaker: Player_Romus
390.text: "Keep on reading. Sounds like there's a lot of useful information in there."

391.speaker: Player_Romus
391.text: "I like his analogy. I'm less convinced about his preferred system of government."

392.speaker: Vina Toras
392.text: "Yes, I've also started to read about Valgslandian Socialism. It makes even more sense to me."

393.speaker: Vina Toras
393.text: "That's why Hegel branched off with Valgslandian Socialism. I've been reading about that as well."

394.speaker: Vina Toras
394.text: "To be honest, a lot of it is outdated. I've also been reading some newer texts about Valgslandian Socialism."

395.speaker: Player_Romus
395.text: "It may be a steady ship, but it sails on the currents of privilege and tradition, not the winds of change and progress."

396.speaker: Player_Romus
396.text: "We do not need a steady ship. We need to recognize the changing seas and adapt to them."

397.speaker: Vina Toras
397.text: "I hope not. Our people still need us."

398.speaker: Vina Toras
398.text: "How can they, without a noble hand to guide them?"

399.speaker: Vina Toras
399.text: "That doesn't need to be the case. Monarchs have embraced change and progress in the past."

400.speaker: Vina Toras
400.text: "Change can be threatening to many people. Our presence on the throne is a symbol of continuity."

402.speaker: Vina Toras
402.text: "They don't belong to everyone in Rizia, though, do they? So much of this coast is private property..."

403.speaker: Player_Romus
403.text: "What have you been doing these days, anyway?"

404.speaker: Vina Toras
404.text: "The usual. Ballgoing. Public appearances. Grandmother enrolled me in an advanced etiquette class."

405.speaker: Narrator
405.text: She reached up and gave her horse a pat on the nose.

406.speaker: Vina Toras
406.text: "It's beautiful here, isn't it? I can see why the Sords had their eye on it."

410.speaker: Player_Romus
410.text: "Do you think it was the right decision to let them build their resort?"

411.speaker: Player_Romus
411.text: "They did indeed. But I showed them who's in charge."

412.speaker: Player_Romus
412.text: "Do you think I should have given it to them?"

413.speaker: Player_Romus
413.text: "That's your own fault. Why don't you find something to do?"

414.speaker: Vina Toras
414.text: "You mean between the ballgoing, the public appearances and the advanced etiquette classes Grandmother's making me go to?"

415.speaker: Vina Toras
415.text: "You just accepted that Sordish resort deal, didn't you? That was entirely your decision."

419.speaker: Vina Toras
419.text: "You just turned down the Sords' offer to build a resort here, didn't you? That was entirely your decision."

420.speaker: Player_Romus
420.text: "It's so beautiful it deserves to be shared."

422.speaker: Vina Toras
422.text: "Sure. I mean, Queen Lyza recognized the importance of being connected with Sordland."

423.speaker: Vina Toras
423.text: "Mother would be rolling in her grave at the news, though. Remember how she always used to call them 'sordid' instead of 'Sordish'?"

424.speaker: Vina Toras
424.text: "It's what Queen Lyza would have done."

425.speaker: Vina Toras
425.text: "A Sordish resort on our shores! Imagine."

427.speaker: Vina Toras
427.text: "Maybe. If only to honor the history of trade between our countries under Queen Lyza."

428.speaker: Vina Toras
428.text: "Mother would've rolled in her grave, though. Remember how she always used to call them 'sordid' instead of 'Sordish'?"

429.speaker: Player_Romus
429.text: "Don't even get me started on what your Aunt Bea calls them."

430.speaker: Vina Toras
430.text: "Mother would've rolled in her grave. Remember how she always used to call them 'sordid' instead of 'Sordish'?"

432.speaker: Player_Romus
432.text: "She had an ear for a good pun."

435.speaker: Player_Romus
435.text: "I honestly don't think about it that often."

437.speaker: Player_Romus
437.text: "You almost died too that day, you know."

439.speaker: Player_Romus
439.text: "Tell me about it. It hurts every time we come back here."

441.speaker: Player_Romus
441.text: "Really? I'll remember that the next time I'm in Derdia."

444.speaker: Vina Toras
444.text: "Some sort of welcome ceremony. But Rizia hasn't had a diplomatic visit to Derdia in decades, so the exact procedure is unknown."

445.speaker: Vina Toras
445.text: "Remember to tell them to treat women like people, too."

446.speaker: Vina Toras
446.text: "They are. Have you heard about how abysmal women's rights are in Derdia? I'm never setting foot there."

449.speaker: Player_Romus
449.text: "What are you up to nowadays, Vina?"

450.speaker: Player_Romus
450.text: "I was only following your late mother's wishes. Remember how she used to call them 'Sordid' instead of 'Sordish'?"

451.speaker: Player_Romus
451.text: "For now, let's just enjoy having this time and this beach to ourselves."

452.speaker: Vina Toras
452.text: "Sure, Father. I don't mean to complain."

453.speaker: Vina Toras
453.text: "It's true. She would have been rolling in her grave if you'd said yes."

454.speaker: Player_Romus
454.text: "Do you agree with it? Should I have turned them down instead?"

455.speaker: Player_Romus
455.text: "That's right. I showed them who's in charge."

456.speaker: Player_Romus
456.text: "Do you think I should have let them build it?"

457.speaker: Player_Romus
457.text: "Yes, and I'm proud of it. A beach as beautiful as this deserves to be shared."

459.speaker: Vina Toras
459.text: "I don't think so. I mean, Queen Lyza recognized the importance of being connected with Sordland."

460.speaker: Vina Toras
460.text: "Mother would be rolling in her grave at the news, though. Remember how she always used to call them 'sordid' instead of 'Sordish'?"

461.speaker: Vina Toras
461.text: "It's what Queen Lyza would have done."

462.speaker: Vina Toras
462.text: "A Sordish resort on our shores! Imagine."

464.speaker: Vina Toras
464.text: "Maybe. If only to honor the history of trade between our countries under Queen Lyza."

465.speaker: Vina Toras
465.text: "Mother would've rolled in her grave, though. Remember how she always used to call them 'sordid' instead of 'Sordish'?"

466.speaker: Player_Romus
466.text: "Don't even get me started on what your Aunt Bea calls them."

467.speaker: Vina Toras
467.text: "Mother would've rolled in her grave. Remember how she always used to call them 'sordid' instead of 'Sordish'?"

469.speaker: Player_Romus
469.text: "She had an ear for a good pun."

476.speaker: Vina Toras
476.text: "But I agree that if the people of this country want revolution, we will not be able to stop them."

477.speaker: Vina Toras
477.text: "But in my opinion, if the people want revolution, we should be the ones who bring it to them."

478.speaker: Player_Romus
478.text: "Is it really revolution if we're still on the throne?"

479.speaker: Player_Romus
479.text: "We Torases are not revolutionaries. We are keepers of tradition."

484.speaker: Player_Romus
484.text: "All right. Keep reading it if that's what you really want."

486.speaker: Player_Romus
486.text: "I'm concerned for your safety. If you're going to harbor these sentiments, then by God be quiet about it."

487.speaker: Vina Toras
487.text: "I will. You're the one who brought up the subject."

488.speaker: Vina Toras
488.text: "But... you're the one talking about getting rid of the monarchy. Would you turn us into Lespia?"

490.speaker: Vina Toras
490.text: "Never mind. You know best, Your Majesty."

491.speaker: Player_Romus
491.text: "The people who want revolution also want to see me dead."

493.speaker: Player_Romus
493.text: "If that is truly what they want, I will not get in their way."

494.speaker: Player_Romus
494.text: "Don't tell me you're still reading Comrade Chavatangakwunua."

501.speaker: Vina Toras
501.text: "No thanks to you. I'm a grown woman and I will read what I like."

502.speaker: Vina Toras
502.text: "Would you have me executed if I said yes?"

503.speaker: Vina Toras
503.text: "Well... um, yes. He makes a lot of good points."

504.speaker: Player_Romus
504.text: "I am warning you, Vina. Stop filling your head with this nonsense."

505.speaker: Player_Romus
505.text: "No need to get defensive. Keep reading it if that's what you really want."

506.speaker: Player_Romus
506.text: "I'm concerned for your safety. If you're going to harbor these sentiments, then by God be quiet about it."

507.speaker: Player_Romus
507.text: "Give me a summary when you have the chance. I'm dying of curiosity."

510.speaker: Vina Toras
510.text: "I don't know what it was like in the '20s. But it does feel like some sort of change is brewing."

511.speaker: Vina Toras
511.text: "Why not? A good monarch adapts to the times."

513.speaker: Vina Toras
513.text: "Not if you're willing to change with them."

514.speaker: Vina Toras
514.text: "I will, I will. You're the one who brought up the topic."

518.speaker: Vina Toras
518.text: "Never mind. You know best, Your Majesty."

532.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
532.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLC.Focus_Government_Reform"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Hugo_KnowsIntention"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true

533.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
533.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Focus_Government_Reform"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Hugo_KnowsIntention"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true) == false

534.speaker: Player_Romus
534.text: "It doesn't matter. You heard what I said to Hugo. It's time for House Toras to step aside and let the people rule."
534.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLC.Focus_Government_Reform"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Hugo_KnowsIntention"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true

535.speaker: Vina Toras
535.text: "So you really mean it. You want to reform the kingdom."

536.speaker: Player_Romus
536.text: "The future is unpredictable. Any one of the other royal houses could seize power at any moment."

538.speaker: Vina Toras
538.text: "Not if you neutralize the threat. Like you were talking about with Uncle Hugo."
538.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLC.Hugo_KnowsIntention"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Focus_Government_Absolutism"] == true

540.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
540.conditionsRaw: Variable["RiziaDLC.Hugo_KnowsIntention"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Focus_Government_Absolutism"] == true

541.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
541.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Hugo_KnowsIntention"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Focus_Government_Absolutism"] == true) == false

542.speaker: Vina Toras
542.text: "That's what you're worried about? Not the people of Rizia seizing power themselves?"
542.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Hugo_KnowsIntention"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Focus_Government_Absolutism"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true) == false)

547.speaker: Vina Toras
547.text: "Nothing, Father. Can we go back to my original question? What would happen if you had a son?"

549.speaker: Vina Toras
549.text: "It can't be that hard to keep the provinces happy. Can it?"
549.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Hugo_KnowsIntention"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.Focus_Government_Absolutism"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Vina_OnCouncil"] == true)

550.speaker: Vina Toras
550.text: "You didn't answer my question. What would happen if you had a son?"

551.speaker: Player_Romus
551.text: "I don't know, Vina. If the situation ever arises, it will be a hard decision."

554.speaker: Vina Toras
554.text: "Thanks. It's lovely to know all my preparations may or may not be in vain."

555.speaker: Narrator
555.text: She uncrossed her arms again with a look of contrition.

556.speaker: Vina Toras
556.text: "Sorry, Father. I do understand the importance of royal tradition. But it's frustrating not to have any power over my lot in life."

557.speaker: Player_Romus
557.text: "If you want agency, you can always take yourself out of the line of succession. If I don't have a son, the crown will go to Hugo when I die. Or more likely, your cousin Ricardus."

558.speaker: Player_Romus
558.text: "This is all completely hypothetical. Just assume that you're my successor and prepare yourself accordingly."

560.speaker: Vina Toras
560.text: "I'm not ready to give up all hope of becoming queen, thank you."

562.speaker: Player_Romus
562.text: "You're a future Duchess and a member of the Royal Council. That's already more power than most Rizians will ever have."

566.speaker: Vina Toras
566.text: "You're right, of course. But you knew you'd be king ever since you were a child. It's different for me."

567.speaker: Player_Romus
567.text: "You're a future Duchess and a member of House Toras. That's already more power than most Rizians will ever have."
